chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man divorces a woman while she is pregnant, he must spend upon her until she gives birth to her child. When she gives birth, he gives her her recompense (for breastfeeding), and he should not cause her hardship, except if he finds someone who is cheaper in recompense than her. If she agrees to that recompense, she is more deserving to breastfeed her son until she weans him.

key_terms.تَضَعَ حَمْلَهَا: She gives birth to her load/child

ai.seo_question: What are the financial and breastfeeding rights of a divorced pregnant woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the financial maintenance (nafaqah) and breastfeeding compensation (ujrah) for a pregnant woman post-divorce, emphasizing the husband's duty to provide until childbirth. It introduces a nuanced economic principle where the husband may reduce costs by hiring a substitute nurse, yet the mother retains priority rights to breastfeed if she accepts the adjusted compensation, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on balancing paternal obligation with maternal rights. This ruling underscores the continuity of care during the transitional period of weaning, ensuring the child's welfare is not compromised by financial negotiations.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazal, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man divorces the woman and she is pregnant, he has to spend upon her until she places her load (gives birth). So when she has place it, he gives her recompense, and should not harm her except if he finds one who is of a cheaper recompense than her (for the breast-feeding). So if she (agrees to) breast-feed with that recompense, she is more deserving with (breast-feeding) her son until she weans him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al- Kinaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man divorces his pregnant wife he must pay for her maintenance until childbirth. When she gives birth, he must pay her wages without causing any harm to her, unless he finds someone who breastfeeds for less. If she also agrees for less then she has the priority to have her son until weaning.’”
